bindings.claim: Gateway routes POST /links, requiring an Idempotency-Key, to the link service, which dedupes retries, checks alias availability, then inserts the immutable mapping into Links DB and write-through populates Redis so the first redirect is already a cache hit.

GET /{code} checks Redis, then the replica on a miss; if the replica also lacks the row (replication lag on a new link) or is down, it falls through to the primary before giving up, so a live link is never 404'd. The click event is emitted with ack+retry, never fire-and-forget.

The dashboard query reaches the decoupled Click Counts Store, refreshed every 30s by a 20-way-partitioned aggregator sized for 10k events/sec peak. Events publish with ack+retry so none are silently dropped; idempotent upserts block double counts; monitoring alerts on backlog or lag.

Hop budget: gateway5+service10+cache5=20ms p99 hit path. A cache miss costs the failed 5ms lookup plus the replica's 15ms = 35ms; if the replica also misses or is down, a further 10ms primary fallback brings the rare double-miss path to 45ms — both under the 50ms budget.

The hot standby, sized for 100% of peak, absorbs cache-miss reads and promotes on primary failure; if it lacks a row or is unavailable, the fallback continues to the primary rather than failing, and a fresh standby auto-reprovisions from the new primary within minutes of promotion.

Click events publish with ack+retry (never fire-and-forget) and a 20-way-partitioned aggregator, sized for 10k events/sec peak, batches them into the Counts Store every 30s with idempotent dedup; monitoring alerts on queue backlog or aggregator lag before the 5-minute bound is at risk.
Links DB is a single Postgres instance indexed on short code; 20 million rows is well within one instance's capacity with headroom before sharding would ever be needed.

At 2,000 rps average nearly all reads hit cache (20ms p99); the replica absorbs residual misses (35ms p99) and the primary is only a last-resort fallback on replica-miss or outage (45ms worst case), so steady load never serializes through the primary in the common case.

At 10,000 rps peak the cache serves most reads, the replica takes 100% of peak on a cache outage with the primary as further fallback, and a 20-way-partitioned queue/aggregator sized for this exact peak rate keeps click counting off the redirect path without backing up.

narrative.overview: The panel's sharpest findings were two relocated SPOFs and a silent-loss gap. First, the redirect's cache-miss fallback went only to the hot standby replica: if that replica itself lacked a just-created row (replication lag) or was simply down, a real link 404'd and the whole availability claim rested on one unredundant replica with no further fallback. I added a second fallback hop from the service straight to the primary, and the primary's endpoint is now a stable, role-based address so writes keep working across a promotion; after any failover a fresh standby auto-reprovisions from the new primary within minutes, so the design tolerates more than one failure a month, not just one. Second, the click-event emit was labeled fire-and-forget: a broker hiccup silently dropped a click with no compensation. The emit now carries an at-least-once ack+retry contract, buffering locally rather than dropping. Third, the single aggregator had no stated parallelism against a 10k/sec peak producer; it's now 20-way partitioned, with monitoring watching queue backlog age and aggregator lag directly. I also corrected the miss-path latency arithmetic — the failed cache lookup's 5ms was missing from the 30ms total — and state the rare double-miss-to-primary cost too (45ms, still under budget). Finally, createLink now requires an idempotency key so a client retry can't duplicate a link, and alias collisions are rejected before insert.

componentRationales.prose: The marketer and the visitor are the same client surface: one issues creates and reads the dashboard, the other just follows redirects. No change requested here.

Still a thin router with a declared 5ms hop budget and metrics emission, now also enforcing idempotency: createLink requires an Idempotency-Key header so a client retry after a timeout can't create a duplicate link before it ever reaches the service.

Still the sole owner of create and redirect logic. dbWriteCreate is now idempotent — keyed by the idempotency key or custom alias, rejecting alias collisions before insert — and emitClickEvent now carries an explicit at-least-once, ack+retry contract instead of a bare fire-and-forget. dbReadFallback is documented as the first fallback only: on a replica miss or outage it falls through to the primary via the new edge to n-5.
Now explicitly write-through on create (via cachePopulate on e-3), closing the gap where a cache that's only ever read can never reach a stated hit rate. No TTL is needed since mappings never change.

Still the system of record for the immutable mapping, but it now also serves as the last-resort read fallback (dbReadFallbackPrimary) when the replica lacks a row or is down, closing the gap where a replication-lag window could 404 a brand-new link. Its address is a stable, role-based endpoint so writes don't need to change when a standby is promoted into this role.

Still a hot standby sized for 100% of peak, absorbing cache-miss reads and promotable on failure — but it's no longer the sole fallback: a miss here now falls through to the primary instead of failing outright, and a fresh standby auto-reprovisions from the new primary within minutes of any promotion, so the design survives more than one failure per monthly window.

Still a durable, at-least-once log, now explicitly partitioned (20-way) so a single consumer can't bottleneck the 10k/sec peak, and its producer contract is now ack+retry with local buffering — a failed publish is retried, never silently dropped.

Still batches every 30 seconds with idempotent, keyed upserts, but now runs with stated consumer parallelism (20, one per queue partition) sized to the peak event rate, so a backlog at 10k events/sec doesn't silently push staleness toward the 5-minute bound.
The counter lives here, fully decoupled from the immutable link row, matching the rule that a hot-row counter must not share a row with the entity it's counting.

Still receives metrics from every redirect-path component, now also from the queue and aggregator, and its config adds explicit freshness alerting — queue backlog age and aggregator lag thresholds — so a stalled count pipeline is caught before a marketer notices stale numbers, not just a p99 or availability breach.

criterionNarrations.prose: Create still flows gateway→service→single immutable insert, now gated by a required idempotency key so a client retry can't duplicate a link, with alias collisions rejected before the insert and the cache write-through populated as before.

Redirect still resolves from cache first, but the fallback is now two-tiered: replica, then primary, so a just-created link within the replication-lag window or a replica outage no longer produces a false 404 — the fallback actually reaches a node guaranteed to hold the row.

The marketer's count still comes from batch aggregation off an event queue, now explicitly partitioned for peak throughput and published with ack+retry so no click is silently lost in transit, with monitoring watching the pipeline's lag directly.

The hop budget is corrected: the failed cache lookup's cost is now included in the miss-path total (35ms, not 30), and the rare double-miss-to-primary path is stated too (45ms) — both still comfortably under the 50ms p99 budget.

The replica is no longer a bare swap for the primary: its own miss or outage now falls through to the primary, and a fresh standby is auto-reprovisioned after any promotion, so the 99.95% claim doesn't quietly rest on tolerating only one failure a month.

The 30-second aggregation interval stays well inside the 5-minute bound, and now that interval is actually protected: ack+retry on emit stops silent event loss, partitioning stops peak-load backlog, and monitoring alerts on lag before the bound is ever threatened.
Unchanged: 20 million indexed rows remains a non-issue for a single Postgres primary; nothing in this revision touches storage volume.

At 2,000 rps average, the corrected arithmetic (20/35/45ms across hit/replica-miss/double-miss) still clears the latency budget, and the two-tier fallback means average load never depends on a single replica holding up alone.

At 10,000 rps peak, the replica remains sized for full peak with the primary as a stated further fallback, and the click pipeline is now explicitly 20-way partitioned for this exact rate, so neither the redirect path nor the counting path backs up at peak.

Unchanged: links are inserted once via dbWriteCreate and never updated; the only addition is idempotent dedup on retried creates, which still produces at most one row per logical link and never alters an existing one.
